function: Adversarial attack on a learned double-RIS MIMO autoencoder, crafted by a PGD-based iterative algorithm (RMAEP) without trained parameters; the learned autoencoder is only the attacked system (p. 4).
notes: The PDF is arXiv:2410.20103v1. Its title and four authors match the Crossref record of the DOI (IEEE Wireless Commun. Lett., 2025). Code no_learning: the method that the paper proposes and evaluates is a white-box adversarial attack. p. 4: "we propose Algorithm 1, named RIS-MIMO adversarial example-based PGD (RMAEP), to optimize the adversarial perturbation vector". Algorithm 1 (p. 3) runs projected gradient descent with a binary search on the perturbation vector and has no trained parameters, although p. 2 says the attack can "learn". The learned part is a 1D-CNN autoencoder whose CNNs set the phase shifts of the two RISs and decode the symbols (p. 2: "We employ one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to replace the physical components of these blocks"). It is only the system under attack (p. 2: "legitimate learning-based devices that can replace the RIS-aided MIMO system and suffer from attackers"). It is never compared with a detection or RIS baseline: all comparisons are between attacks, on the SER (p. 5: "RMAEF [8], the jamming attack [12], and the secured system (no attack) [7]"). For the reviewer: if RMAEP counts as learned, the code becomes function, because an adversarial attack is a security function (like anti-jamming) outside the seven areas. If the victim autoencoder counts as the method, the work would be included in area 1, since the main metric is the SER (Nt = Nr = 16, two RISs of 32 elements, p. 4).
